biggest_gpu_eaters: Resolution Scale 100% at DLAA = rendering at FULL native 2560x1440 (no upscaling savings)
Shading Quality: Epic = maximum shader complexity per pixel
Materials: Epic = highest texture detail + parallax mapping
Post Processing: Epic = full chain (bloom, AO, SSR, volumetrics)
Depth of Field: Epic = cinematic DoF with bokeh (expensive when active)
Light Shafts: Enabled = volumetric god rays (medium cost)
DLSS Frame Gen 2x = GPU generates extra frames (uses VRAM + tensor cores)
free_or_cheap: Motion Blur: 0% = FREE (disabled, no GPU cost)
Async Compute: Enabled = actually SAVES time (fills GPU bubbles)

dlss_breakdown.DLAA: Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing — renders at native res, uses AI for AA only (no upscaling). Most expensive DLSS mode because no resolution savings.
dlss_breakdown.Frame_Gen_2x: Tensor cores generate 1 fake frame between each real frame. Doubles apparent FPS. Uses ~500MB VRAM + adds 1 frame latency.
dlss_breakdown.why_replace_over_time: DLSS is NVIDIA proprietary neural network. As Gaia learns GPU behavior, she could model the quality/performance tradeoff herself — predicting which settings give the best visual per watt.

toggle_schedule.philosophy: Toggle ONE setting at a time, play for 2-3 minutes, screenshot the FPS counter. This gives Gaia paired samples: setting_change → performance_delta.
suggested_order: 1. DLAA → DLSS Quality (biggest single FPS gain, ~30-40%)
2. Frame Gen 2x → OFF (see real FPS without AI frames)
4. Post Processing: Epic → High (removes heavy SSR/volumetrics)
7. Depth of Field: Epic → Off (gain when active)
8. Materials: Epic → High (mainly VRAM, small FPS)
9. HDR: Off → On (test if monitor supports it — EI322QUR should!)
toggle_schedule.frequency: Every 5-10 min toggle ONE, play, screenshot. Gaia digests each pair.
